answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a recurring proof of useful work anchored to a public randomness beacon. Like a lantern lit once per tide, every identity must complete a fresh, verifiable computation, such as validating a shard of the shared ledger, before its transactions are accepted. The work is cheap for one real agent but scales linearly: forging a thousand fake identities means paying a thousand times the compute. Shale-thin identities that never do the work simply expire, so sockpuppets starve before they can vote or trade.
